commitResults.messageTitle: feat: rename Duke to hermes-mini and add greet-and-exit
commitResults.messageBody: Rename the starter chatbot Duke -> hermes-mini (class HermesMini) and implement Level 0: print the ASCII banner, greet the user, then say goodbye and exit. Fill the AGENTS.md student-profile blanks and fix the Java-version note to match this machine (JDK 26 via java_home, no sdkman). Refresh README/docs Duke references and ignore *.class files.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: echo user commands and exit on bye
commitResults.messageBody: Add a read-eval loop that echoes each command entered (framed by dividers) until the user types "bye", which prints the farewell and exits. Adopt the canonical indented message format (4-space divider, 5-space content) and update the README example to match.

feat: added children of Task to supports 3 types of tasks

Rewrite in rust because I like rust
Implement GUI version of app in rust version
Add JavaFX interface for Hermes Mini
commitResults.messageBody:
Hermes Mini exposes its task logic through terminal input and output.
This prevents a graphical interface from reusing command handling
without duplicating behavior.

Add a shared response API and compose it with a JavaFX front end. Keep
the terminal interface as a thin adapter so both interfaces retain the
same commands, persistence, and responses.

Add a Gradle wrapper and JavaFX build configuration so the graphical
application has a reproducible entry point.
Move all console output and formatting into a dedicated Ui class. This separates presentation concerns from command handling while preserving the chatbot's observable behaviour.
Move task-file loading, parsing, and saving into Storage. Keep HermesMini focused on coordinating commands while preserving the existing persistence format and error behaviour.
Extract Parser and TaskList to complete the A-MoreOOP increment. HermesMini now coordinates Ui, Storage, Parser, and TaskList while preserving command behaviour.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update gitignore to include some debugger configs
refactor: organize classes into duke package
commitResults.messageBody: Place all application classes under the duke package while keeping src/main/java as the Java source root.

commitResults.messageTitle: build: add Gradle build and run configuration
commitResults.messageBody: Configure the Java and application plugins, Java 25 toolchain, Maven Central repository, and duke.HermesMini application entry point.

commitResults.messageTitle: test: add JUnit coverage for parser and task list
commitResults.messageBody: Configure JUnit Jupiter in Gradle and add meaningful tests for Parser date and argument handling and TaskList operations, indexing, and capacity limits.
Add the Shadow plugin and configure hermes-mini.jar with duke.HermesMini as its executable entry point.
Document remaining fields, constructors, enum construction, and parser/task-list responsibilities so public APIs and non-trivial helpers are clearly described.
The project needs a reusable reference for SE-EDU Java naming, layout, comments, and control-flow conventions. Add a project-local skill so future Java changes follow the same rules.
The project needs a reusable reference for imperative subjects, concise bodies, and what-and-why commit explanations. Add a project-local skill for future commits.
Future work must apply the project-specific Java and Git skills. Record those requirements in the repository agent instructions so they are visible to every contributor and coding agent.
Task.java contains tab-indented members and a non-standard field comment. Replace the tab indentation and clarify the path comment so the Java source follows the project coding standard.

The task list and storage rely on valid task inputs at their internal boundaries. Add assertions to document those assumptions and add a Java 25 GitHub Actions workflow that builds and tests every push and pull request.

Task serialization and keyword matching contain repetitive collection loops. Use streams for both operations, normalize matching with Locale.ROOT, and centralize the task capacity constant to make the code clearer and safer.
Users need a lightweight way to record a task with a reminder time. Add the remind command and persist reminder tasks using the existing task and storage abstractions.

The chatbot is limited to terminal output and does not distinguish user messages, normal replies, or errors visually. Add a resizable Swing interface with asymmetric alignment, compact spacing, and highlighted errors while retaining the existing command engine.
The chatbot uses generic task-manager phrases that do not reinforce its identity. Adopt a concise messenger theme across greetings, confirmations, errors, farewell text, and the GUI error treatment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle malformed and duplicate task input
commitResults.messageBody: Whitespace variations, incomplete commands, duplicate tasks, and invalid event ranges can produce confusing results. Normalize command spacing, report missing parameters precisely, reject duplicates, and require event start times to precede end times.

Parser normalization, duplicate detection, task state, dated task formatting, and persistence were not covered by tests. Add focused JUnit cases for those behaviors, including mixed-task storage round trips in an isolated temporary directory.

Users need concise instructions for every command, data persistence, and common recovery steps. Replace the placeholder guide with a complete Hermes guide and add a representative full-window interface image for the product website.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate plain and executable JAR outputs
commitResults.messageBody: The regular JAR and Shadow JAR write to the same output path, which Gradle 9 rejects as an implicit task dependency. Give the regular JAR a plain classifier so each task owns a distinct artifact.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show Gradle build status in README
commitResults.messageBody: The repository has automated Gradle checks, but their status is not visible from the project landing page. Add a workflow badge so contributors can immediately see whether the latest build passes.
Expose the passing Gradle workflow from the repository README.

The Level 10 branch contains the earlier GUI increment but is not part of master history. Record the required branch merge while preserving the newer finalized Hermes implementation already on master.

The submitted Swing executable did not meet the Level 10 requirement and
the project could not be rebuilt with the documented Gradle wrapper
command.

Implement the interface using the JavaFX tutorial structure, including a
separate launcher, FXML controllers, dialog boxes, and cross-platform
JavaFX dependencies. Restore the Gradle wrapper and cover the shared
command-response path with automated tests.

The Shadow JAR now includes JavaFX runtimes for Windows, macOS, and Linux
and remains compatible with Java 25.
